system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

Application: Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) - Patient Experience
Dear Verdane Care hiring team,
Your Patient Experience role connects two areas of my work: accessible React interfaces and
booking experiences. I am a First Class Honours Computing graduate with professional fron-
tend experience and full-stack project experience using TypeScript, Node.js, Express and Post-
greSQL. Verdane Care’s focus on making appointment booking and follow-up simpler for pa-
tients is a strong match for the usability and accessibility work I can bring to your team.
During my internship at Harbourline Media, I resolved accessibility audit findings across more
than 20 React components, addressing keyboard navigation, colour contrast and ARIA labels.
I also built a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery, documented it in Storybook
and wrote unit tests with Jest and React Testing Library. My interest in accessibility began
when a friend who uses a screen reader showed me the barriers she encountered online. That
experience gives particular meaning to your commitment to WCAG 2.2 AA.
For my final-year project, Tidewatch, I built a React and TypeScript application backed by a
Node.js/Express API and PostgreSQL. The API cached public weather and tide data, while
the database stored user favourites. I tested the application with NVDA and VoiceOver and
achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100. My backend experience comes from projects;
my professional work has focused on frontend development, including a freelance Next.js yoga
studio website with a timetable and emailed booking requests.
Iwouldbringpracticalaccessibilitywork, reusablecomponentdevelopmentandautomatedunit
testing to your squad. Helping approximately 30 first-year students in web development labs
also gave me experience supporting others as they learned. I would welcome the opportunity to
discuss how this foundation could contribute to your patient-facing features. My portfolio and
GitHub links are included above. Thank you for considering my application.
Yours sincerely,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
